visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 at least presents a coherent arithmetic-sum-to-area visual with π and total-area expression, while Lesson 2 has a blank title screen and a malformed, nonsensical formula/subtitle that does not accurately represent the math.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have absent gate specs and absent plan JSON, so neither provides any functional checkpoints or input-rendering gates.

narration_quality.rationale: Both lessons have absent narration transcripts, so neither demonstrates clearer pacing, cleaner phrasing, or fewer audio defects than the other.

sync.rationale: Both lessons have no transcript or timing data available, so neither provides any evidence of better or worse synchronization than the other.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Neither lesson provides a lesson plan or transcript, so there is no available teaching content to compare for mathematical accuracy or pedagogical clarity.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a coherent, centered, legible notebook-style layout with consistent visuals, while Lesson 2 begins with an essentially blank title screen and later shows awkward/garbled subtitle text despite a large equation.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner because the only non-tie dimension verdicts both favor it, with high confidence: visual_accuracy preferred Lesson 1 at 0.9 and polish preferred Lesson 1 at 0.95. The remaining four dimensions were ties, mostly because both lessons lacked transcripts, timing data, gate specs, or lesson plans, so they provide no counterweight in favor of Lesson 2. Since Lesson 2 received no dimension wins and was specifically criticized for blank/garbled visuals, Lesson 1 wins, though confidence is moderated by the lack of evaluable evidence in narration, sync, interactivity, and concept accuracy.
